title: Give the ops console's commands the right status

blocks.text: The warehouse's ops console lets an operator type a command, such as `reserve SKU-7731 12`, and runs the public method of that name on a handler object. The console colours its reply by status, and the on-call rota is paged for every 500. Operators complain that a typo in a quantity pages someone, while a quantity typed as a word gets an answer that blames the command.
`call(...)` already finds the method. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Dispatcher.java`:

items: `run(method, args)`: call the method on the handler and turn what happened into a `Reply`.

rows: the arguments don't fit the command's parameters
500, the simple class name of what it threw

cases.says: a command that completes answers 200 with its result, and one that fails answers 500 with the name of the exception it threw, checked or unchecked
an IllegalArgumentException thrown by the command itself answers 422 with the command's message
arguments of the wrong type or number answer 400, not 422, although the call fails with an IllegalArgumentException

origin.section: Method.invoke Wraps the Method's Exceptions and Throws Its Own Argument Errors Unwrapped

concepts: Method.invoke wraps whatever the method throws, checked or unchecked, in InvocationTargetException, while its own refusal of unfitting arguments is an unwrapped IllegalArgumentException.
